newsitem.title: USA: General Magic unveils new software.
newsitem.headline: General Magic unveils new software.

text.p: General Magic Inc said Wednesday it will release next month new versions of its software for controlling handheld computers, just as Microsoft Corp is entering the same software niche.

The Sunnyvale, Calif.-based software company said the updated version of its Magic Cap program will feature better access to the Internet and will run on devices that use less expensive electronics. In late morning trading, General Magic shares rose 1/4 to 3-1/8.
General Magic, founded by three former Apple Computer Inc executives in 1990, was one of the first companies to chase the fledgling handheld computer market, but has yet to make a profit from it.

Meanwhile, Microsoft, the world's biggest personal computer software company, is aggressively rolling out software, dubbed Windows CE, for a new generation of cheaper, more powerful, paperback-sized computers. The new computers, however, cannot run General Magic's software.

"The Magic Cap operating system addresses the specific needs of people who are unfamiliar with or not interested in using traditional personal computers, or the new Windows CE devices," said Steve Markman, General Magic's chief executive.
General Magic said it will pitch the software to people in fields such as health care and transportation who need small computers and do very specific computing tasks.
